scenario: [LTIM.12.11]: no wall-clock time is resolved to an instant, so a zone's transitions leave no gap or overlap: each instant reads one local time, at the offset of the one `TimeZoneOffset` fact answering it ([LTIM.10.7]). Three `Europe/Paris` rows over 2024's two transitions: +3600 from 2024-01-01T00:00Z until 2024-03-31T01:00Z, +7200 from there until 2024-10-27T01:00Z, and +3600 from there until 2025-03-30T01:00Z. `show` binds `z = e.t.local("Europe/Paris")` and writes it through `::String` ([LTIM.8.2.4]), one Event per pump. Spring-forward: fact 1, 2024-03-31T00:59:59Z, is `2024-03-31T01:59:59+01:00`, and fact 2, one second later at 01:00:00Z, is `2024-03-31T03:00:00+02:00`: the local hour 02 is never read. Fall-back: fact 3, 2024-10-27T00:30:00Z, is `2024-10-27T02:30:00+02:00`, and fact 4, 01:30:00Z, is `2024-10-27T02:30:00+01:00`: the repeated wall clock is two instants, each at its own offset. A runtime that does not take a fact at its own `valid_from` writes no `2 2024-03-31T03:00:00+02:00`: it reads fact 2 through the earlier row, `2024-03-31T02:00:00+01:00`, a skipped local time, or finds no answer and faults DOMAIN ([LTIM.10.5.3]). PATH PINNED: libds's `adapter_ds_local` (rete/adapters.c) through `ds_rete_tz_resolve` (rete/wm_rete.c), rendered by `render_time` (rete/eval.c) through `ds_rete_local_split`; Mercury's `ds.eval.ltim_3_2_local`, rendered by `ds.format.render_time`.
rules_ds:
schema E scope logical:
    id: Int key
    t: Time mutable

rule show:
    E e
->
    let z = e.t.local("Europe/Paris")
    let s = z::String
    log info "{e.id} {s}"
